title: The 99 Plus One album and Mustard Greens
summary: His own album with a big band including James Booker and George Davis, recorded at Cosimo's.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Oh, okay. Okay. You did make a record.

We had an office on Arlene Street. And we did the tune, 99 plus one. It made a little noise, it made enough noise for them to come back to make an album. And then at that time, for you to make an album, it had to sell it. And then I didn't get, I didn't write 99 plus one. Wardell wrote the tune. I had a tune on that album called Mustard Greens. As a matter of fact, a friend of mine just gave me an album of it. I really lost that album too. So I have a copy of that. It's mostly instrumental. It's not necessarily a drum take off. Excuse me, a drum solo. A lot of it's with a big band. It's with about 15, 16 pieces of bands. James Booker's playing, and Warren Bell, Emory, Thomas. This was done at the Old Cosmo on Beverly Nicholas Street. But it's with a big band. I got a chance, huh?
Well, I think I've got a copy in the back of 99 plus one.
That's just it. That's George Davis on the guitar. George Davis on the guitar.
Yeah. So you had a great crew. Oh, yeah.
All qualified musicians. And I just thought I can't think of all the guys that was on. Three or four trumpets, three trombones, five saxophones, and rhythm.
